title: The Exam: Overview
summary: Everything about Cambridge IGCSE ESL 0510: the three papers, marks and weightings, every Paper 1 exercise, how writing is marked, listening and speaking, a 2-hour time plan and a 10-week revision plan.

blocks.text: This page is your map of the whole Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language exam. Read it before anything else. It tells you which papers you will sit, how long each one is, how many marks every exercise carries, how the writing is marked, and how to plan your time and your revision. Parents will find a short Arabic explanation at the end.
The qualification in one paragraph

**Cambridge IGCSE English as a Second Language** tests four skills: **Reading, Writing, Listening and Speaking**. Reading and Writing are tested together in **Paper 1**. Listening is **Paper 2**. Speaking is **Paper 3**. The same course is offered under different **syllabus codes**. The code decides two things: the grading scale (A*-G or 9-1) and whether your Speaking mark counts towards your final grade. Many Year 9 and Year 10 students in Egyptian British schools are entered for **0510**, so this course is written for 0510, but the papers are the same for the other codes.

rows: Speaking is **separately endorsed**: it does not count in your overall grade. Your certificate shows a separate Speaking grade from 1 (highest) to 5.
**Count-in Speaking**: Speaking is worth 25% of your overall grade.
Speaking is separately endorsed as Distinction, Merit or Pass.

blocks.title: Check your code with your school
blocks.text: Your school chooses the code when it enters you for the exam. Ask your teacher or the exams office which one you are taking. Some schools in Egypt also offer a different, Egypt-only syllabus (**0465**, a Core syllabus graded C-G) with a shorter Paper 1 (1 hour 45 minutes) and shorter writing tasks (100-150 words). This course is for 0510/0511 - if you are entered for 0465, the reading skills here still help, but your paper is different.
The three papers at a glance

rows: Four reading exercises (30 marks) and two writing exercises (30 marks). You write on the question paper. All questions are compulsory. No dictionaries.
About 50 minutes (including 6 minutes to transfer answers)
Five exercises, 40 multiple-choice questions. You hear each recording twice and shade your answers on an answer sheet.
A one-to-one test with your teacher or an examiner: an interview, a short talk and a discussion. It is recorded.

blocks.text: Look at the weighting for 0510: **Paper 1 is worth 70%** of your grade and Listening 30%. That means reading and writing together decide most of your result. Spend most of your revision time on Paper 1 - but do not ignore Listening, because 30% is a lot of marks to lose.

blocks.title: Key facts to remember
items: Paper 1: 2 hours, 60 marks, 6 exercises (Exercises 1-4 reading, Exercises 5-6 writing).
Paper 2: about 50 minutes, 40 marks, 40 multiple-choice questions, every recording played twice.
Paper 3: about 10-15 minutes, 40 marks. For 0510 it gives a separate grade from 1 to 5.
There are **no tiers** any more: everyone sits the same papers.

blocks.text: No more Core and Extended

Before 2024, students were entered for either **Core** or **Extended** papers. Core students could not get the top grades. Since the first exams in **2024**, this **tiering has been removed**. Every student sits the same Paper 1, the same Listening paper and the same Speaking test, and **every student can get any grade from A* to G**. This is good news: you do not need to choose a level, and a strong performance on the day can take you all the way to A*.

blocks.title: Old books and websites
blocks.text: If a book, video or website talks about 'Core paper', 'Extended paper', 'form-filling' or 'summary writing', it is describing the old exam. Use it only for general practice, and always check its question types against the table on this page.
Grades and what they mean

items: **Overall grade (0510):** A*, A, B, C, D, E, F or G. Below G is 'ungraded'. It is worked out from Paper 1 and Paper 2 only.
**Speaking grade (0510):** a separate grade from **1 (high) to 5 (low)**, shown on the certificate when the standard is met.
**Grade boundaries** (how many marks you need for each grade) are set by Cambridge after every exam series. They change a little each time, so nobody can promise you an exact number before the exam.
Cambridge links the grades to the international CEFR scale. Roughly, an overall **grade C plus a Speaking grade 2** is about **B2** level - the level of a confident independent user of English.

blocks.text: Paper 1, exercise by exercise
Paper 1 is the most important paper, so you need to know every exercise by heart. Each exercise has its own page in this course.

rows: One text of about 400-450 words (for example an article, a blog or a web page)
Short answers - a word, a phrase or a number. Q1-5 need one answer each, and Q6 needs three answers.
About 600-650 words: one text in up to five sections, or up to five short texts (for example four young people writing about a hobby)
Multiple matching: you write the letter of the section or person that matches each statement (9 statements)
Note-making: complete short notes under two headings (7 bullet points in total). An example is given.
About 550-600 words, for example a blog or an article
Multiple choice with three options (A, B or C): main ideas, details, the writer's attitude and opinions
A short task with three bullet points
Writing: an **informal email** (for example to a friend or relative), about 120-160 words
A short task with comments or a picture
Writing: a formal or semi-formal **article, report, essay or review**, about 120-160 words

blocks.text: Add it up: reading = 8 + 9 + 7 + 6 = **30 marks**, and writing = 15 + 15 = **30 marks**. Total **60**. The reading exercises test four skills: finding specific facts, understanding how ideas and opinions connect, choosing the right details for a purpose, and understanding what is implied (meant but not said directly).

blocks.title: How reading answers are marked
items: One mark for each correct answer, whole marks only.
Marking is **positive**: you are not punished for small spelling or grammar mistakes in reading answers - unless the mistake makes your meaning unclear or changes the word.
For short answers and notes, the mark scheme lists the acceptable answers. Extra words are not needed, so keep answers short.
For multiple choice and matching, only the correct letter gets the mark.

blocks.text: How the writing is marked

Both writing exercises use **exactly the same marking criteria**. Each task is marked out of 15: **Content out of 6** and **Language out of 9**. The examiner reads your answer, decides which band fits it best, and then chooses a mark inside that band. Marks are given for what you do well, not taken away for each mistake.

rows: Task fulfilment: did you answer all parts of the task, stay relevant, use the right style for the text type, and keep the reader and purpose in mind? Development: are your ideas explained and expanded?
Range and accuracy: how wide and how correct is your vocabulary and grammar? Organisation: is the writing in a clear order, with paragraphs and a good range of linking words?
5-6: task fully done, everything relevant, style right all the way through, ideas very well developed
7-9: skilful, with common and less common words, simple and complex sentences, very accurate grammar and clear organisation with many linking devices
3-4: task generally done, mostly relevant, style generally right, ideas generally developed
4-6: clear, with mostly common words and some less common ones, mostly simple sentences with some complex ones, and errors that do not usually block meaning
1-2: task only partly done, style not right, little development
1-3: meaning not always clear, with only simple words and sentences and errors that make it hard to understand

items: **Word count:** both tasks ask for **about 120-160 words**. There is no automatic penalty, but writing far less usually means weak development, and writing far more wastes time and often adds mistakes and irrelevant ideas. Aim for 140-160.
**Exercise 5** is always an **informal email**.
**Exercise 6** can be an **article, a report, an essay or a review** in a formal or semi-formal style. Learn all four - especially the essay, which many students forget.

blocks.text: Paper 2 Listening: the five exercises
The whole Listening paper is multiple choice. You hear every recording **twice**. At the end you have **6 minutes** to copy your answers onto the answer sheet.

rows: Choose one of four pictures (A-D) for each question
Two questions per extract, three written options (A-C)
One talk or presentation by one speaker
Complete 8 sentences by choosing from three options (A-C)
Match each speaker to one of 8 statements (two statements are not used)
8 questions with three options (A-C) about the main speaker

blocks.text: Total: **40 questions, 40 marks**. The listening pages in this course explain how the wrong options (distractors) are built to trick you, and how to avoid them.
Paper 3 Speaking: the parts

Speaking is a one-to-one test of about **10-15 minutes** with your teacher or an examiner. It is recorded, marked by your school and checked (moderated) by Cambridge. You may not take written notes into the test.

rows: The examiner explains the test and checks your details.
The examiner asks you set questions on a topic.
You get a card with a topic and talk on your own.
The examiner asks discussion questions linked to the Part 2 topic.

blocks.text: You are marked out of 40: **Grammar 10, Vocabulary 10, Development 10 and Pronunciation 10** (pronunciation includes intonation - the music of your voice). For 0510 this gives your separate Speaking grade. For 0511 it is 25% of your overall grade.
What changed in 2024 (briefly)

items: Core and Extended tiers were removed: one set of papers for everybody.
Paper 1 became one 2-hour Reading and Writing paper with 60 marks and 6 exercises (4 reading, 2 writing).
The summary-writing task was removed. Exercise 4 is now a multiple-choice reading exercise.
Listening became 100% multiple choice: 40 questions, 40 marks, about 50 minutes.
Speaking went up from 30 to 40 marks and now has three marked parts. You only see a card for Part 2.
The writing mark scheme changed: both tasks are now Content 6 + Language 9.

blocks.text: The syllabus for 2027-2029 keeps the same structure, so everything on this page should still apply in the next few years. Always check the latest syllabus with your school.
Time plan for the 2-hour Paper 1

Cambridge does not tell you how long to spend on each exercise - you must manage the 2 hours yourself. Below is the plan I recommend to my students. It gives reading and writing about the same time, because each is worth 30 marks, and it keeps 10 minutes at the end for checking.

rows: Short text, answers mostly in order
Longest text: you must compare several writers
Details are spread across the whole text
Long text, and the options need careful checking
5 min plan, 17 min write, 3 min check
Harder style: 5 min plan, 20 min write, 5 min check
Blank answers, spelling of copied words, word count

blocks.title: Two rules for timing
items: Wear a watch and write your 'finish' times at the top of the paper at the start (for example, if you start at 9:00, Exercise 1 ends at 9:12, Exercise 2 at 9:27...).

Never leave an answer blank. A sensible guess in multiple choice or matching can still win the mark. If you are stuck, guess, mark the question with a small star and come back in the final 10 minutes.

blocks.text: Some students prefer to do the writing first, while they are fresh. That is allowed - you may answer the exercises in any order. If you do this, keep the same times and be strict: do not let the writing eat into your reading time.
How to use this course
The pages are in a sensible order. Work through them from top to bottom the first time, then go back to the pages for your weakest exercises.

rows: Exam overview (this page), Core reading skills
The exam, and the twelve reading skills every exercise depends on
How each exercise works, a step-by-step method, traps, timing and an original practice test with answers
Writing overview, Informal email, Article, Report, Review, Essay
The criteria, structure, openings, closings, useful phrases, common mistakes and full-mark model answers for every genre
Listening overview, The five listening exercises
How each exercise works and how to beat the distractors
Each part of the test and how it is marked

items: **Study actively.** Do every practice question before you click 'Show answer'. Write your answer on paper first.
**Keep a mistakes notebook.** For every wrong answer, write the question, your answer, the right answer and *why* you were wrong (for example: 'I copied too much', 'I chose the first number I saw').
**Learn vocabulary in pairs.** Paper 1 rewords everything. When you learn a word, learn a synonym with it (*buy - purchase*, *start - launch*).
**Write by hand.** The exam is on paper. Practise your writing tasks by hand and count your words.

blocks.text: A 10-week revision plan
This plan assumes about **4-5 hours a week**. If you have less time, keep the order but shorten the practice. If your exam is closer than 10 weeks, combine two weeks into one.

rows: Read this page and the Core reading skills page. Do all the skill practice. Do one Exercise 1 practice with no time limit to find your level.
Study the Exercise 1 page. Do the practice test in 12 minutes. Write down every mistake type in your notebook.
Study the matching method. Do one practice in 15 minutes. Practise finding paraphrases of opinions.
Study note-making. Practise writing short notes (2-5 words) under headings. Watch spelling of copied words.
Study multiple choice and attitude words. Do one practice in 15 minutes. For every option, write why it is right or wrong.
Read the Writing overview and the Informal email pack. Learn the structure and phrases. Write two emails (25 minutes each) and check them against the checklist.
Study both packs. Write one article and one review (30 minutes each).
Study both packs. Write one report and one essay. Compare the four styles: who is the reader in each?
Study both listening pages. Do listening practice every day (even 15 minutes). Practise a 2-3 minute talk on familiar topics with a family member or friend.
Do one full Paper 1 in exactly 2 hours and one listening paper. Mark them. Spend the rest of the week only on your two weakest exercises.

blocks.title: Every week, whatever the focus
items: Learn 15-20 new words with a synonym for each.
Read one English article or blog for pleasure (sport, science, technology - anything you like).
Listen to 15 minutes of clear spoken English (a podcast or the news).
Re-read your mistakes notebook.

blocks.text: Quick check

items.q: How long is Paper 1, and how many marks is it worth?
For 0510, what percentage of the overall grade is Paper 1?
items.a: 70%. Listening is 30%. Speaking is separately endorsed (0%).

items.q: Does the Speaking test count towards a 0510 grade?
items.a: No. It is separately endorsed with its own grade from 1 (high) to 5 (low). For 0511 it counts 25%.

items.q: How many marks is Exercise 1, and how many answers does Question 6 need?
items.a: 8 marks. Questions 1-5 need one answer each, and Question 6 needs three answers.

items.q: Which text types can appear in Exercise 6?
items.a: An article, a report, an essay or a review (formal or semi-formal).

items.q: How is each writing task marked?
items.a: Out of 15: Content 6 + Language 9. The same criteria are used for Exercise 5 and Exercise 6.

items.q: How many times do you hear each listening recording?
Can a student who would once have taken 'Core' get an A* now?
items.a: Yes. Tiers were removed from 2024, so everyone sits the same papers and can get any grade from A* to G.

blocks.title: لأولياء الأمور: الامتحان في دقيقة
items: امتحان IGCSE English as a Second Language (كود 0510) فيه ثلاث أوراق: الورقة الأولى قراءة وكتابة (ساعتان - 60 درجة - 70% من التقدير)، والورقة الثانية استماع (حوالي 50 دقيقة - 40 سؤال اختيار من متعدد - 30% من التقدير)، والورقة الثالثة محادثة (Speaking).
في كود 0510 المحادثة لا تدخل في التقدير النهائي، بل تُكتب في الشهادة كتقدير منفصل من 1 (الأعلى) إلى 5. أما في كود 0511 فالمحادثة تمثل 25% من التقدير. اسألوا المدرسة عن الكود الذي سُجِّل فيه ابنكم.
لم يعد هناك مستوى Core و Extended منذ 2024، وأصبح كل الطلاب يمتحنون نفس الورقة ويمكنهم الحصول على أي تقدير من A* إلى G.
أهم ما يساعد ابنكم: قراءة يومية بالإنجليزية، حفظ كلمات مع مرادفاتها، كتابة موضوع أسبوعيًا بخط اليد في الوقت المحدد، والاستماع للإنجليزية 15 دقيقة يوميًا.
